clue.text: Substance? Cover it in sauce

indicators.note: in places the cover and the following word inside the sauce

parts.note: soy is a salty sauce used in Asian cooking
a lid covers a pot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether there is substance to a dish and is told to smother it in sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidity is firmness or real worth, the quality of having substance behind it.

clue.text: Elastic cut during second attempt

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: during places the cut inside the attempt, as an event inside a span of time

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to etch is to cut lines into a surface

explanation.surface: A rubber band snaps on someone's second go at using it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy can be pulled out and spring back, like elastic.

clue.text: Worthy arrangement of family run without force

definitions.note: used as a noun: a worthy person

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so these letters are reordered
without means the letter for force is left out

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, once trimmed
F is the physics symbol for force; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A worthwhile set-up for a family business that runs without coercion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worthy' reads as an adjective, but it is the noun: a worthy is a notable person.
explanation.definitionFit: A luminary is an eminent, respected figure, which is what a worthy means as a noun.

clue.text: Fool about, getting covered by mound of sand

indicators.note: getting covered by means put underneath and enclosed by the mound

parts.note: a dune is a hill of sand
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A clown messing around on the beach gets buried in sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool about' reads as the phrase for messing around, but fool is the definition and about gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow-witted person, a fool.

clue.text: Change technique, climbing with son for miles in country

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an art is a skill or technique

indicators.note: in puts the preceding run of words inside the country

parts.note: a nation is a country
S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A climber changes method, travelling with their son for miles across a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A transformation is a thorough change in form or character.

clue.text: Pain shown by saint with restless desire

parts.note: standard abbreviation for saint
an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: A martyred saint suffers pain from an unsettled longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side, typically felt while running.

clue.text: New companion admitted to proper working club

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside the word for proper

parts.note: true means proper, correct
N is the abbreviation for new
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A newcomer is accepted into a proper, active club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society joined by members; it is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short thick stick carried by police, a type of club.

clue.text: Heart in aromatic kernel

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the phrase that follows

parts.note: the end of aromatic and the start of kernel

explanation.surface: The core of a fragrant nut.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart looks like the centre of the kernel; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the heart, because it beats like a clock.

clue.text: Keeping quiet about severe defeat

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent about a crushing loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding means concealing something, and informally a hiding is a heavy beating or trouncing.

clue.text: Complicated lines gain title for eggheads

indicators.note: complicated means twisted and tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Tricky dialogue earns honours for the academics.
explanation.definitionFit: The intelligentsia are the intellectual class; egghead is a jokey word for a bookish intellectual.

clue.text: Back in prison, amoral type

indicators.note: back tells us to read the concealed letters from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the tail of prison and the head of amoral, read backwards

explanation.surface: A wicked character is returned to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amoral type' looks like a description of a villain, but type alone is the definition: the upright typeface as opposed to italic.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman is the ordinary upright style of printing letters, a typeface contrasted with italic.

clue.text: Demolition of cannon due to be reported

indicators.note: demolition knocks things down, leaving the letters to be rebuilt in another arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The scrapping of a cannon is expected to be made public.
explanation.definitionFit: Something announced has been made known publicly, the same as being reported.

clue.text: State view, following notes, right away

indicators.note: following puts the word for view after the trimmed word for notes, not before it
away says the letter standing for right is taken out

parts.note: tenners are ten-pound notes
R is the abbreviation for right; this letter is removed
to see is to view

explanation.surface: Someone states a view after reading notes, then leaves directly.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note. 'Following' puts the view after the notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Completely cold and thin

parts.note: C for cold, as on a tap
lean means thin

explanation.surface: Someone is described as entirely chilly and skinny.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean is used as an adverb meaning entirely, as in 'clean forgot' or 'clean through'.

clue.text: Demanding push to create space for emergency stops

parts.note: a hard task is a demanding one
to shoulder is to push with the shoulder

explanation.surface: An insistent shove clears room so that emergency vehicles can halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The hard shoulder is the British name for the paved strip along a motorway's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers may only pull onto the motorway strip beside the lanes when broken down or in an emergency.

clue.text: Fake jewellery's ending in battered tin chest

indicators.note: battered means beaten out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
ending asks for only the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of jewellery
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Imitation gems end up in a dented metal box.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letter goes in among the letters of the box before they are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthetic means artificial or man-made, not genuine, so fake.

clue.text: Old one, team's leader, held in honour

indicators.note: held in means placed inside the honour

parts.note: OBE is Officer of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
sole means one and only

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of team

explanation.surface: A veteran team captain is decorated with an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete describes something outdated and no longer in use, hence old.

clue.text: Treacherous? Yes, we all converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are reformed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asked whether they were disloyal, a group admits they all changed sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaselly means sly and untrustworthy, like the weasel of folklore, so treacherous.

clue.text: In a maul, being knocked about beyond belief

indicators.note: things knocked about are thrown out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugby player caught in a maul is battered to an incredible degree.
explanation.walkthrough: A maul is a rugby scrum-like tussle for the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimaginable things cannot be pictured or credited, so they are past believing.

clue.text: Article on boat going north and south continually

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a yawl is a two-masted sailing boat
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature about a vessel sailing back and forth without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Always means at all times, without stopping, which is continually.

clue.text: Caper, risky venture by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: a gamble is a risky venture

explanation.surface: An escapade that sounds like a dangerous undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caper' suggests a heist; here it means a playful skip.
explanation.definitionFit: To gambol is to skip and leap playfully, the same as to caper.

clue.text: Lead attack filled with energy

indicators.note: filled with means the following letter is put inside the attack word

parts.note: to lash out is to attack
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A charge led from the front is full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead attack' reads as leading a charge; lead is in fact the dog's tether.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead and a leash are both the strap used to walk a dog.

clue.text: Determined airman, one in number over America

parts.note: ten is a number
AC is aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank
Roman numeral one
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A resolute pilot is one of a group flying over America.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are not in clue order: the number comes first, then airman, one, over and America.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenacious person holds firm and refuses to give up, which is being determined.

clue.text: Land identified by mate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a country in East Asia
second meaning: a friend, in Cockney rhyming slang

explanation.surface: A country is recognised by its partner.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, china plate rhymes with mate, so a china is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a large Asian country, and in London rhyming slang it means a pal.

clue.text: Wretched rat caught by a large superior bird

indicators.note: caught by means held inside the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a boss is a superior at work

indicators.note: wretched suggests something in a sorry, mangled state, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A miserable rodent is seized by a big, dominant bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is a huge seabird with the largest wingspan of any bird.

clue.text: Perfect island, compact

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island
a compact is an agreement, a deal

explanation.surface: A small, tidy island seems flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compact' reads as an adjective meaning small, but it is the noun for an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, the best that could be wished for.

clue.text: Comfort thus given by fabric

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: A soft material provides consolation in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation offered to someone in distress, which is comfort.

clue.text: Very bad rage, beset by utter brutality

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded on all sides by the word that follows

parts.note: to utter is to say
V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: bad here means gone wrong, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Terrible fury surrounded by total cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning total, but it is the verb to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Savagery is fierce, cruel violence, the same as brutality.
